extracted.intended_audience: State air agencies, state plan developers, owners/operators of affected EGUs, utilities, reliability authorities, and stakeholders participating in CAA section 111(d) state plan development
extracted.subtask_short: state plan development for EGU emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for states to develop, submit, and demonstrate implementation of state plans under EPA emission guidelines for existing electric generating units (EGUs), including meaningful engagement, transparency, reporting, and compliance-assurance provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Meaningful Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: “timely engagement with pertinent stakeholders and/or their representatives in the plan development or plan revision process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should not be disproportionate in favor of certain stakeholders and should be informed by available best practices. This definition was finalized in subpart Ba revisions (Nov 2023) and applies to state plan development under these emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Pertinent Stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Pertinent stakeholders “include, but are not limited to, industry, small businesses, and communities most affected by and/or vulnerable to the impacts of the plan or plan revision.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects inclusion of communities most affected by climate change, communities near affected EGUs and pipelines, energy communities and energy workers (operation, maintenance, construction, fuel extraction and delivery, CO2 transport and storage), balancing authorities, system operators, reliability coordinators, and potentially stakeholders in neighboring states or Tribal lands when EGUs are near borders. States should use state- and source-specific knowledge to refine identification and consider cumulative burdens and overburdened communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of Meaningful Engagement in State Plan Submittal
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must describe how the state provided meaningful engagement with pertinent stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the state must include: (1) a list of the pertinent stakeholders identified by the state; (2) a summary of engagement conducted; (3) a summary of the stakeholder input received; and (4) a description of how stakeholder input was considered in plan development or plan revisions. EPA will review these items for completeness; missing elements may render a submission incomplete or grounds for disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced Participation and Focus on Vulnerable Communities
rubrics_metrics.description: When designing engagement, states should allow for balanced participation, including communities most vulnerable to plan impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should recognize and engage communities that may not have had a voice historically and prioritize outreach to overburdened communities, considering cumulative pollution burdens and multiple stressors that may increase vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Strategy: Timely, Transparent, Accessible Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: States should develop an engagement strategy ensuring information is available in a timely and transparent manner with adequate and accessible notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet notice alone may be insufficient; states should consider additional, prominent advertising channels (e.g., newspapers, libraries, schools, hospitals, travel centers, community centers, places of worship, gas stations, convenience stores, casinos, smoke shops, Tribal Assistance offices, clinics) and address geographic, linguistic, and other participation barriers. States should share information and solicit input on plan development and accompanying assessments/analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EPA and Federal Resources to Identify Stakeholders and Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: States are encouraged to use EPA tools and federal resources to assist in stakeholder identification and impact analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include unit-level proximity analyses (population within 5 km and 10 km), the Power Plant Environmental Justice Screening Methodology (PPSM), EJScreen, and the Energy Communities Interagency Working Group Clearinghouse. These tools provide demographic, exposure, and environmental burden data to help identify impacted or vulnerable communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Regional and Cross-Border Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: States should consider regional implications and collaborate when EGUs are located near state or Tribal borders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be reasonable to identify pertinent stakeholders in neighboring states or Tribal lands and to coordinate with the relevant air pollution control authority to conduct meaningful engagement addressing cross-border impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement on Facility- and Community-Specific Circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful engagement should elicit input on facility- and community-specific issues related to emissions control systems, including CCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should solicit stakeholder input on specific implementation concerns and consider exposure to chemical and non-chemical stressors, local conditions, and the potential cumulative burden on communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Energy Communities and Workforce Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: States should include energy communities and affected energy workers as pertinent stakeholders and consider workforce impacts in planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States are encouraged to consider federal programs for employment and training assistance, to promote workforce data transparency, and to include workforce-related data (e.g., expected number and type of jobs, required skills) in meaningful engagement and plan analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Reliability Authorities in Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: States should include balancing authorities, system operators, and reliability coordinators in engagement due to their authority over electric reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing visibility into unit-specific compliance plans (early notification and periodic follow-up on decisions like control technology installation and voluntary cease-operation choices/timeframes) helps reliability authorities plan and address potential reliability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Publicly Accessible EGU Websites
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must require owners/operators of affected EGUs to establish publicly accessible 'Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs' websites posting all reporting and recordkeeping information for each affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information to post includes emissions data; items relevant to determining compliance with standards of performance; increments of progress, reporting milestones, and milestone reporting (including milestones for units planning to permanently cease operations); any extension requests and approvals; and other plan-submittal information. Data should be available in a readily downloadable format. EPA concluded this is not duplicative of other reporting programs because these emission guidelines include unique reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Deviations from Increments of Progress or Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must report any deviation from any federally enforceable state plan increment of progress or reporting milestone within 30 business days after discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must explain the cause(s) of the deviation, describe all measures taken or to be taken to cure the deviation and prevent recurrence (including timeframes), be submitted to the state regulatory agency, and be concurrently posted to the affected EGU's Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for EGUs Planning Permanent Cessation — Initial Report
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-fired steam generating EGUs that plan to permanently cease operation before Jan 1, 2032 (and are otherwise exempt), owners/operators must submit an initial report to EPA five years before planned cessation or by state plan submission date, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial report elements: (1) summary of process steps required to permanently cease operation (approximate timing/duration and notification requirements); (2) supporting regulatory documents (correspondence and official filings with RTO/ISO/balancing authority/PUC or other authorities; deactivation-related reliability assessments; SEC filings mentioning EGU plans; integrated resource plans and PUC orders; reliability analyses; notifications altering timing of deactivation). These reports are required under CAA section 114(a) and limited to reporting (no milestones for exempt units).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for EGUs Planning Permanent Cessation — Annual and Final Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must submit annual status reports for each remaining year prior to planned cessation and a final report after cessation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports must include: (1) progress on each process step identified in the initial report; (2) supporting regulatory documents demonstrating progress toward steps; and (3) new regulatory documents and relevant SEC filings since the prior report. Final report (no later than 6 months after committed closure date) must document actions taken post-cessation to ensure permanence, including regulatory filings and decommissioning plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Comply with State and Federal Decommissioning/Shutdown Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans that include EGUs planning to permanently cease operation must require those EGUs to comply with applicable state and Federal requirements for permanent cessation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes removal from the state's air emissions inventory and amending or revoking all applicable permits to reflect permanent shutdown status. The requirement reinforces existing state and Federal law necessary for transparency and orderly administration of emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of Enforceable Commitments to Permanently Cease Operation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not requiring that commitments to permanently cease operation be expressed as an emission limit of 0 lb CO2/MWh; states have discretion on the form of enforceable commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such commitments may be codified in state regulation, permit, order, or other legal instrument and submitted with the state plan. If an emission limit or other requirement creating an enforceable commitment is included in a Title V permit before plan submission, it must be labeled 'state-only' until EPA approval (then revised to be federally enforceable). EPA emphasized including state instruments reflecting intent because state instruments can be revised without corresponding plan revisions; including them in the plan is necessary to preserve the guidelines' integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Plan Submission Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must be submitted 24 months after publication of the final emission guidelines in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA superseded the default subpart Ba timeline (18 months) and set 24 months for this rule due to the complexity of the source category and need for extensive coordination among states, utilities, reliability authorities, and owners/operators. EPA also noted final rule differences that reduce burden (fewer affected units than proposed; exclusion of combustion turbines; no co-firing with low-GHG hydrogen as BSER).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism Authority for States
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include in their state plans a short-term reliability mechanism allowing affected EGUs to comply with an emission limitation corresponding to their baseline emission rate during grid emergency periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is intended to allow states to respond quickly to emergency situations and avoid affected EGUs being out of compliance or needing administrative compliance orders (ACOs) during emergencies. EPA concluded states and EGUs will not need to rely on ACOs for such emergencies given these mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA Stance on Administrative Compliance Orders (ACOs) for Reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing the proposed approach to use ACOs to address grid reliability risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA noted commenters' concerns about practicality, timeliness, and potential negative implications of ACOs, and instead relied on structural changes and mechanisms (e.g., short-term reliability mechanism) in the final rule to address reliability.
